### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/organizations`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **35** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/organizations/src/ensure-default-organization.ts`, `packages/plugins/organizations/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-defaults/data.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/field-level-security.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/index.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx`  _(via SYSTEM_CTX (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/ui/forms.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via SYSTEM_CTX (symbol, a top-level const object))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/organizations/src/ensure-default-organization.ts`, `packages/plugins/organizations/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-defaults/data.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **151** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8d05456cbe03667ea2352c9a99e67d4a862a8294` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5a2967aaf080e1579310eff933136f09c2775b32` — the merge of head `2c1dd397bfc7c161eb1f110638e3ef73e6533c3d` into base `8d05456cbe03667ea2352c9a99e67d4a862a8294`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5a2967aaf080e1579310eff933136f09c2775b32 && git checkout 5a2967aaf080e1579310eff933136f09c2775b32
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8d05456cbe03667ea2352c9a99e67d4a862a8294 2c1dd397bfc7c161eb1f110638e3ef73e6533c3d && git checkout -B drift-repro 8d05456cbe03667ea2352c9a99e67d4a862a8294 && git merge --no-ff 2c1dd397bfc7c161eb1f110638e3ef73e6533c3d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8d05456cbe03667ea2352c9a99e67d4a862a8294
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8d05456cbe03667ea2352c9a99e67d4a862a8294` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · `domain:spec` seat 2 (#18549) · session `session_01LFqdRsuM5nkqoJdHd5ztVk` · 2026-10-15T04:01Z

This is the seat review of record for #23354 (claim `6182191596`, dev report `6184063982`) on head:

`70a9ae6008bb5dd324dd6acb9f20e28cf7ff5529`

It is not the contract review. That review is owed at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` and runs next.

1. **Form.**
   - Draft to `main`. The first line is `Fixes #23354`, and `Clause-②: yes` sits at the start of a line.
   - The only closing keyword names this card. The body's mention of #23054 carries no verb.
   - No `content/docs/releases/` change.
   - 31 files, +1701/−414, so under the 3000-line threshold.
   - No governed path: `scripts/adr-anchors/**` is not one.
2. **Premises measured.** The dev confirmed hypotheses 1–3. Hypothesis 4 was wrong, and the dev corrected it: the organizations twin needs the per-organization replay's rows, which the boot settle does not carry. So the replayer in `app-plugin.ts` records them. The correction stands.
3. **Gates.**
   - Check-runs on this head at this read: 38 in all, 17 success, 5 skipped, 16 in progress, none red.
   - Locally the dev ran 121 of the 125 derived families. The other 4 are NOT MEASURED, each with a reason.
   - Ready and enqueue wait for every check to be green.
4. **Accepted deviations.**
   - The file surface went beyond the claim. Each step was measured and is named in the PR body:
     - the per-organization replayer and the basic-insert fallback in `app-plugin.ts`;
     - the binding in `organizations-plugin.ts`;
     - a docblock in `ensure-default-organization.ts`;
     - one anchored alias in `organizations/vitest.config.ts`;
     - rows in `engine-double-contract.pinned.json`.
   - This record amends the claim's surface to the PR's file list.
   - The twin's paging fallback is removed. The removed symbols (`claimUnowned`, `isPerRowHookBudgetRefusal`, `idsFrom`, `MAX_CLAIM_PAGES`, the module's `CLAIM_PAGE_ROWS`) were all module-private. The exported `claimOrgSeedOwnership` stays.
   - Declared narrowing, per the seat's lock notes: every `test:repo` project and the whole runtime and spec suites are left to CI.
5. **Out-of-scope findings.**
   - (1) cloud-connection's fallback seed-replayer records no replay rows. The carrier is this PR's contract review, as the dev's open question 2.
   - (2) InMemoryDriver's `$in` cost goes in the Acceptance notes. It is a driver property, recorded in the claim's docblock.
   - (3) An `ignore`-mode dataset reports a row its key matched. This goes in the Acceptance notes.
6. **Changeset sentences checked against the diff.**
   - `landedIds` defaults to `[]` (`seed-loader.zod.ts:423`).
   - `seededRecordIds?(object, organizationId?)` is optional (`contracts/seed-settlement.ts:137`).
   - `publishLanded` is called at `app-plugin.ts:1797`, `:1874` and `:1894`.
   - `CLAIM_PAGE_ROWS = Math.floor(MAX_BULK_PER_ROW_HOOK_ROWS / 2)`.
   - `bootstrapPlatformAdmin` gains the `seededRecordIds` option (`:246`).
   - The bump levels (`spec`, `metadata-protocol` and `runtime` minor; `plugin-security` and `organizations` patch) are the contract review's ② to judge.
7. **Landing terms.**
   - First a contract review PASS at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on the head, then every check green, then the seat marks the PR ready and enables auto-merge.
   - `needs:contract-review` stays on this PR until then.
   - The dev's two `open_questions` go to the review's ③.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `70a9ae6008bb5dd324dd6acb9f20e28cf7ff5529`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #23354 (body and all ten comments, rulings and earlier records included); PR #23605 (body, the 31-file list, the net diff against its merge base `32e03d2fd` with `main`, which stood at `16abea88` at this read); the check-runs on this head, read at 2026-10-15T04:15Z. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**Face and tier.** The file list carries a published schema (`packages/spec/src/data/seed-loader.zod.ts`) and a published contract (`packages/spec/src/contracts/seed-settlement.ts`), so the review is owed at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. No governed path: `scripts/adr-anchors/**`, `.changeset/**` and `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` are not register rows. Head repo equals base repo.

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong:

1. **`SeedLoadResultSchema.landedIds`** (`z.array(z.string()).default([])`, described) — a widening: a result without the key still parses, one carrying it now parses. `SeedLoadResult` is the schema's `z.input`, so the TypeScript field is optional and no implementer's literal breaks. The generated outputs were regenerated (`authorable-surface/data.json`, `authorable-defaults/data.json`, `content/docs/references/data/seed-loader.mdx`) and `Spec property liveness` concluded success. RIGHT.
2. **`ISeedSettlementService.seededRecordIds?(object, organizationId?)`** — an optional member: an existing implementer still satisfies the interface, a consumer gains one read. The two readings (boot-time sources without `organizationId`; the most recent per-organization replay with it) and the "absent means no reading, not an empty seed" rule are stated in the docblock. `check:api-surface` runs in `Type Check · consumer gates` (concluded success) and its baselines track export names (`ISeedSettlementService (interface)`, `SeedLoadResultSchema (const)` both pre-exist), so no baseline regeneration was owed. RIGHT.
3. **`@objectstack/runtime` `SeedSourceHandle`** — a package-entry type export — gains a REQUIRED `publishLanded(report)`. The handle is produced only by `declareSeedSource`; consumers call it and nothing outside the runtime implements it, so this is judged right at minor. Named for the record: a hand-rolled value typed `SeedSourceHandle` outside this repo stops type-checking; an optional member was the strictly additive spelling and was not required. `SeedLandingReport` and `recordOrganizationReplay` are not re-exported from the entry, so no further surface is added. RIGHT.
4. **`claimSeedOwnership` NULL arm** — `owner_id IS NULL` becomes `owner_id IS NULL AND id IN (one chunk of the seeded ids)`, one write per chunk of `CLAIM_PAGE_ROWS` (half the per-row hook ceiling); the `usr_system` arm is unchanged, and the diff's premise holds (no guest door, form door or runtime writer stamps `SystemUserId.SYSTEM`; the dispatch pin claims `SEED_IDENTITY` rows). Without a reading the NULL arm re-owns nothing and the pass report says so, which is fail-closed toward ADR-0138 D1 and never the old predicate. The function is a package-entry export: its options widen (an optional field) and its default-path behaviour changes, which is the fix and is stated in the changeset under "Direct callers". RIGHT.
5. **`bootstrapPlatformAdmin`** gains the optional `seededRecordIds` pass-through on a non-exported options interface; both callers (`claimSeedOwnershipOnSettle` and the `kernel:ready` promotion) bind the reading through the published contract (`readSeededRecordIds`), lazily per object, so an over-budget seed is covered by the `app:seeded` re-run as before. RIGHT.
6. **`claimOrgSeedOwnership`** takes the same selector, bound per organization by `OrganizationsPlugin` from the same contract; the `ql.find` precondition is dropped (a widening of the engines it accepts); without a reading it returns nothing and says so once. The #23054 paging fallback is removed rather than kept: a chunk predicate matches at most as many rows as it carries ids, at most half the ceiling, so the refusal it answered cannot occur, and the 10 500-row guarantee is re-pinned on a real engine. The removed symbols (`claimUnowned`, `isPerRowHookBudgetRefusal`, `idsFrom`, `MAX_CLAIM_PAGES`, the module `SYSTEM_CTX`) were module-private. The deprecated `ensureDefaultOrganization` wrapper hands over no row; its docblock and the changeset say so. RIGHT.
7. **Producer.** `landedIds` is read off `internalIdByRecordIndex`, the per-dataset map every write site already fills through `noteLanded` (insert flush, self-reference write, update, replay skip, refused update of a matched row), deduplicated in record order; a dry run reports none. Pinned on the real loader in `seed-loader-landed-ids.test.ts` (insert, skip replay, update replay, reference-keyed match reporting the resolved id, unseeded row never reported, refused insert, two records one row, dry run). RIGHT.
8. **Host.** The inline seed publishes before `settle()` on the loader path and on both basic-insert fallbacks; the per-organization replayer records through `recordOrganizationReplay`. The tracker keeps `bootLanded` additive and `lastReplay` single. Pinned in `seed-settlement.test.ts` and `app-plugin.seed-landed.test.ts` (loader path, fallback, second-boot re-report excluding a guest row, per-organization record). RIGHT.
9. **ADR anchor.** `scripts/adr-anchors/packages__plugins__plugin-security__src__security-plugin.ts.json` gains ADR-0138 and a D1 invariant sentence that matches the code it anchors (carrier note 6158485388). RIGHT.
10. **Logging.** An `id IN` list is reported by its size (`whereForLog`), never inlined. RIGHT.
11. **Dispatch limits held.** `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` untouched; the `app:seeded` payload in `contracts/plugin-lifecycle-events.ts` untouched. RIGHT.
12. **The three pins triage set (6158407363).** (a) a seed row is claimed on the first boot and on a later boot's replay: `claim-seed-ownership-seed-settle-rerun.test.ts` through the real `SecurityPlugin`, `claim-seed-ownership-warm-boot.test.ts` over a real `ObjectQL` on `SqlDriver` across two processes. (b) a guest-written row and a public-form row keep no owner across two boots: the same two files, `claim-seed-ownership.test.ts`, the organizations unit test and both real-engine dispatch pins; this is the one pin with a red leg under the old predicate, as the first dev's note said. (c) a hook-, flow- or rule-owned row keeps its owner: a preservation pin in the same files. RIGHT.
13. **Measured cost.** The NULL arm now pays `InMemoryDriver`'s quadratic `$in` once, on the pass that claims the rows (measured 2.6 s at 5 000 rows), and nothing on a warm boot; SQL drivers were not measured and the docblock says so. Accepted as a driver property.

**Check-runs on this head**, 44 in all at the reading above: 31 success, 8 skipped (path-filtered or opt-in), 0 failure, 5 in progress. Concluded and judged as the gate verdicts: Lint & Repo Gates and its lanes (which carry `check:test-source-alias`, `check:where-matcher`, `check:engine-double-contract` and the anchor gates), Type Check · source gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · workspace and the TypeScript Type Check aggregate, Spec property liveness, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Build Core, Build Docs, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Documentation Links, `Test Core (5/6)`, and the card and claim guards. NOT MEASURED by this record: `Test Core (1/6)`, `(2/6)`, `(3/6)`, `(4/6)` and `(6/6)`, still running. Those five stand between this verdict and the landing: the seat's landing terms (6184105830 §7) and the Post-Task rule require every check green before the PR leaves draft or is queued, and this PASS substitutes for none of them.

### ② Semver level

- **`Clause-②: yes`** sits at the start of a body line, with no arm — well-formed (at most one arm) and true to the diff: items 1 to 3 widen a published schema, a published contract and a runtime handle; nothing narrows an accept set; no export is removed or renamed, so no breaking changeset, no FROM → TO mapping and no ADR-0087 marker is owed. `skip-changeset` is not applied, correctly: five released packages publish.
- **`.changeset/23354-seed-landed-rows.md`** — `@objectstack/spec` **minor**: RIGHT (items 1 and 2; `yes` takes at least minor). `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` **minor**: RIGHT (a new field on every per-dataset result; additive). `@objectstack/runtime` **minor**: RIGHT (item 3, a required member on a handle only the package constructs, plus the tracker's new read; nothing removed).
- **`.changeset/23354-seed-claim-seed-rows.md`** — `@objectstack/plugin-security` **patch**: RIGHT (a bug fix in a released package; the option widens; the default-path change is stated). `@objectstack/organizations` **patch**: RIGHT (the same; the deprecated wrapper's change is stated; the module-private removals are not surface).
- Both bodies carry what an upgrading reader greps for: the new names, the direct-caller behaviour, and the seed writers outside the claim's purpose.
- Base drift: the branch merged `main` once at `32e03d2fd`; CI ran on the merge of this head into `16abea88` (the drift check's tree line), with no conflict reported. The queue leg re-merges.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Dev deviations (6184063982), each:**
1. File surface exceeded — `app-plugin.ts` beyond the settle hand-off (the per-organization replayer must record or the twin has no reading; the fallback must publish or its seed rows go unclaimed), `organizations-plugin.ts` (the binding), `ensure-default-organization.ts` (docblock), `organizations/vitest.config.ts` (an alias `check:test-source-alias` demanded), `engine-double-contract.pinned.json` (`--write` rows). ANSWERED: each is load-bearing or gate-demanded; the seat amended the surface to the file list (6184105830 §4); accepted.
2. The twin's paging fallback removed, not adapted. ANSWERED: unreachable by construction (①.6); accepted.
3. Lock-pressure narrowing — the whole `runtime` and `spec` suites, `cli` unit, `cloud-connection` and every `test:repo` project left to CI. ANSWERED: CI's `Test Core` shards are the gate; one of six has concluded success and five are in progress, so they are NOT MEASURED here; the landing waits on them.
4. `main` merged once and moved since. ANSWERED: see ②; the queue re-merges.
5. Model-free commit trailers. The AGENTS.md form; nothing to judge.

**Open questions (the dev's two in 6184063982; the PR body's three):**
- **Q1, the per-organization reading keeps the most recent replay only.** ANSWERED, not escalated: accept A as built. The bound is stated in the contract docblock, the one reader (the default organization's owner bind) asks in the call that created the organization, and the failure mode when another replay lands in between is D1's empty state plus an info line, never a guest row handed over. Noted for a later card, not owed here: consuming the per-organization entry on read would close that window at the same memory.
- **Q2, an organization that existed before this process, or a bind retried on a later boot, has no reading.** ANSWERED: accept A. The behaviour it replaces was the defect; the residual (an organization whose creating boot's bind failed keeps its seed rows unowned) is fail-safe and logged, with no measured demand, so no card is filed now.
- **Q3, `cloud-connection`'s fallback `seed-replayer` records nothing** (also out-of-scope finding (a), whose carrier was this review). ANSWERED: accept A for now. The composition (an `OrganizationsPlugin` owner bind on a kernel where only that fallback replayed) has no measured instance; under it the bind hands over nothing and logs it. The owning seat files a card on the first measured instance; the carrier moves from this review to that measurement.

**Seed writers that emit no `app:seeded`** (package-install seed apply, publish-time seed apply, the dev hot-reload seeder, the marketplace install's inline seed) — triage asked that any one that must be reached is carried, not dropped (6182011415). JUDGED: none must be reached. The claim's declared purpose is handing the boot seed to the first admin; those writers run after a human exists (an admin installs or publishes) or in development, and under D1 their rows' owner stays as the writer left it. The changeset names them, which is the carrier.

**Out-of-scope findings:** (a) is Q3. (b) `InMemoryDriver`'s quadratic `$in` — accepted, no carrier; a driver property, measured and recorded in the claim docblock. (c) an `ignore`-mode dataset reports a key-matched row it did not write — accepted as the loader's matching rule; named residual: a pre-existing unowned row whose natural key collides with an `ignore`-mode seed record counts as the seed's and is claimed; the loader's key rule owns that, not this claim.

**Triage's acceptance added after this head (6184093292):** "a runtime-created unowned row keeps `owner_id = null` across a restart" — PINNED on a real engine: `g1` across two SQLite processes in the warm-boot file, `guest_row` and `form_row` across two boots through the real `SecurityPlugin`; HotCRM's `crm_case` queue is exactly this shape. "…and a criteria share keyed on it still reaches its audience" — NOT PINNED in this diff: it exercises `plugin-sharing`'s unchanged `owner_id == null` criteria evaluation and follows from the pinned half, and this diff touches no sharing code. Not a contract defect of this head; the consumer measurement on objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2116 against the first prerelease carrying this fix is where that half is read. Named, not blocking.

**Carrier note 6158485388** — APPLIED (①.9).

**Gap named, not blocking:** the `OrganizationsPlugin` binding (`readSeededRecordIds(ctx, organizationId)`) has no plugin-level test. The tracker side (`seededRecordIds('crm_case', 'org_a')`) and the claim side are each pinned, and the read mirrors the landed shape of `readSeedSettlementSnapshot`; a booted-stack pass over the default organization's owner bind is the measurement that would close it, and the Dogfood Regression Gate concluded success on this head.

**Docs drift advisory (6184053472):** five hand-written pages are listed through the `SecurityPlugin` and `SYSTEM_CTX` symbols; this diff changes no documented behaviour of either (plugin-security's `SYSTEM_CTX` is unchanged, the organizations file's own was removed). The tenant-audit census row for `claim-seed-ownership.ts` (`UNTYPED_RECEIVERS`, the `ql: any` writer) still describes the file. Nothing owed.

**Governed surfaces:** none in the file list, so Prime Directive #14's tiers do not bind this PR; this record is owed by the `Clause-②: yes` schema-and-contract face and the `needs:contract-review` label.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2c1dd397bfc7c161eb1f110638e3ef73e6533c3d`

The earlier record `6184275111` (PASS on `70a9ae600`) and the seat's ACCEPT `6184105830` were read as inputs; neither governs this head. What moved since `70a9ae600` is one file, `packages/runtime/src/seed-datasets.test.ts` (+16/-3), a test fake; no production line moved. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**Face and tier.** The file list carries a published schema (`packages/spec/src/data/seed-loader.zod.ts`) and a published contract (`packages/spec/src/contracts/seed-settlement.ts`), so the review is owed at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong:

1. **`SeedLoadResultSchema.landedIds`** (`z.array(z.string()).default([])`, described) is a widening: a result without the key still parses, one carrying it now parses. `SeedLoadResult` is `z.input` of the schema (`seed-loader.zod.ts:431`), so the TypeScript field is optional; the only producer literal in the repo is `SeedLoaderService.loadDataset` (a grep for `referencesDeferred:` outside tests hits only the schema itself), and `buildEmptyResult` returns `results: []`. The three artifacts the key touches were regenerated: `authorable-surface/data.json`, `authorable-defaults/data.json`, `content/docs/references/data/seed-loader.mdx`. `json-schema.manifest/data.json` is a name-only ratchet that already lists `data/SeedLoadResult`, so no change was owed there. `Type Check · source gates`, which carries `check:authorable-surface`, `check:docs` and the `check:generated` reconciliation, concluded success; so did `Spec property liveness`.
